data.long_meaning: Keya is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kāy', which means 'desire' or 'longing'. In Hindu mythology, it is also the name of a nymph or apsara, who personifies desire and longing in the human heart. The name is often given to girls who are believed to embody these qualities. The name Keya carries the meaning “Desire, Longing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Keya usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, longing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
